summary: Sets out the administrative policies for running remote printer facilities in the tpc.int subdomain. It covers ways to recover costs and discusses auditing, security, and denial of access.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 1529 sets administrative policies for remote printer servers in tpc.int. It discusses ways to recover operating costs, what operators may log, and how they may deny access.

questions: what policies governed tpc.int remote printing
subtitle: Administrative policies for remote printer servers in the tpc.int subdomain.

tldr.problem: Remote printer servers consume resources, while the person initiating an email-to-fax request may not be identifiable with certainty.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 1529 describes community-service, commercial, and sponsored operating models, along with limits for audit logs, privacy rules, and source-based access denial.
tldr.outcome: The memo provides administrative policies for tpc.int remote printer facilities and obsoletes RFC 1486.

today: RFC 1529 is an Informational memo that obsoletes RFC 1486. It describes administrative policies for remote printer servers in the tpc.int subdomain.

sections.title: Remote Printing by Email
sections.content: The tpc.int facility lets a user email a message to an address containing the phone number of a G3-compatible facsimile device. A remote printer server routes the message to the device and sends an acknowledgment to the initiator. RFC 1529 covers administration; the technical procedures are defined in RFC 1528.
sections.plainLanguage: A user sends email that a server delivers to a fax machine. This memo sets policies for operating that service, rather than its technical transfer procedure.

sections.title: Three Models for Recovering Costs
sections.content: The Community Library model provides the service without recovering costs from participants. The Neighborhood Grocery model involves a commercial organization contracting with fax owners to register numbers. The Local Newspaper model allows a third-party sponsor to be acknowledged on a cover sheet and in a notification; if money changed hands, the cover sheet should identify a paid advertisement.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo describes free community service, a commercial service bureau, and a sponsored model. Each handles the service's costs differently.

sections.title: Auditing, Privacy, and Access
sections.content: A server should keep an audit and security log containing at most the listed message and call details. The memo says logs must not be disclosed unless required by legal authority, and not for marketing. Operators may deny access based on source for legal reasons or abuse, but not based on destination; a denial should notify the initiator of the policy violated.
sections.plainLanguage: Operators may keep limited logs for accountability, but should protect them from disclosure and marketing use. They may block a source for legal reasons or abuse, not a destination number.
